meta.title: ERP Selection for Companies | Cyrrus
meta.description: ERP selection consulting: we define, evaluate, and choose with you the ERP that best fits your processes — a 100% vendor-agnostic evaluation.

hero.title: ERP selection and evaluation
hero.description: Choosing an ERP isn't choosing software. It's choosing how your company will run for the next several years. We help organizations define, evaluate, and select the ERP that best fits their processes, objectives, architecture, and investment capacity.

dolor.title: When the ERP stops keeping up with the business

items.title: Business growth
items.description: The company grew faster than the platform holding it up.

items.title: Disconnected systems
items.description: Multiple systems that don't talk to each other, with duplicated information.

items.title: Manual processes
items.description: Parallel spreadsheets to cover what the ERP doesn't solve.

items.title: Poor financial visibility
items.description: Consolidating operations takes weeks instead of being available in real time.

items.title: Obsolete current ERP
items.description: The platform stopped getting real support or scaling with the operation.

items.title: Expansion to new units or countries
items.description: The current ERP can't support the complexity of growing into new geographies.

dolor.narrativa: The ERP that worked when the company was smaller can become a constraint once the organization grows.

problemaReal.title: Deciding to change ERPs is easy. Picking the right one is hard.
problemaReal.body: SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Infor, NetSuite, and many other platforms can solve similar problems from different angles.
problemaReal.punch: More features doesn't mean a better fit.

solucion.title: We determine which ERP your organization actually needs
solucion.linkLabel: This is how we apply the full CIRA Method to software selection

evaluamos.title: We evaluate the ERP from six perspectives

items.title: Functional
items.description: Can it support the business's financial, commercial, logistics, and production processes?

items.title: Technical
items.description: Can it integrate with the current technology architecture without friction?

items.title: Economic
items.description: What's the total cost of ownership, not just the initial license?

items.title: Strategic
items.description: Can it support growth and expansion into new units or countries?

items.title: Vendor
items.description: Who will be behind the platform over the next five years?

items.title: Adoption
items.description: Will the organization actually use it, or will it end up underused?

entregables.title: From uncertainty to a decision you can back up

faq.question: How long does an ERP selection process take?
faq.answer: As a reference, the CIRA method's Identify phase typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, from the strategic kickoff through contracting support.

faq.question: We already have an ERP and aren't sure it's the right one
faq.answer: We evaluate your current platform against the same six objective criteria, even if changing vendors isn't on the table — sometimes the answer is to optimize, not replace.

meta.title: CRM Selection for Companies | Cyrrus
meta.description: CRM selection consulting: we design the evaluation around your real sales process, to choose the CRM your sales team will actually adopt.

hero.title: CRM selection and evaluation
hero.description: A CRM shouldn't force your sales team to change how they sell. It should help them sell better. We help organizations define, evaluate, and select the CRM that best fits their sales process.

dolor.title: When the customer relationship is fragmented

items.title: Scattered information
items.description: Customer data lives in emails, spreadsheets, and each salesperson's memory.

items.title: Leads that fall through
items.description: Sales opportunities lost because no one followed up in time.

items.title: Manual follow-up
items.description: Every salesperson manages their pipeline their own way, with no standard process.

items.title: Poor pipeline visibility
items.description: Sales leadership doesn't know in real time how the month is closing.

items.title: Different tools per team
items.description: Sales, marketing, and service work in systems that don't talk to each other.

items.title: Information tied to people
items.description: When a salesperson leaves, the history of their customer relationships leaves with them.

dolor.narrativa: Low sales traceability doesn't just cost deals — it makes it impossible to measure what's actually working.

problemaReal.title: The challenge isn't finding a CRM. It's finding one your organization will actually adopt.
problemaReal.body: A CRM can have 200 features — but if the sales team doesn't use it, the investment fails.
problemaReal.punch: Fit with the real sales process matters more than the feature list.

solucion.title: We design the selection around your sales process
solucion.linkLabel: This is how we apply the full CIRA Method to software selection

evaluamos.title: We evaluate the CRM from six perspectives

items.title: Functional
items.description: Does it cover lead management, opportunities, pipeline, and customer service?

items.title: Technical
items.description: Does it integrate with marketing, telephony, and existing sales systems?

items.title: Economic
items.description: What's the cost per user and the total cost as the sales team scales?

items.title: Strategic
items.description: Does it support omnichannel, analytics, and AI to keep up with sales growth?

items.title: Vendor
items.description: How solid is the vendor's support and partner ecosystem?

items.title: Adoption
items.description: Does it fit the way your team actually sells, or does it impose a new one?

entregables.title: The right CRM for your sales model
entregables.closingQuote: The result isn't "this CRM is the best." It's "this CRM best answers our requirements and objectives, and here's why."

faq.question: How long does a CRM selection process take?
faq.answer: As a reference, the CIRA method's Identify phase typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, from the strategic kickoff through contracting support.

faq.question: Our sales team already rejected a CRM before — how do we avoid that happening again?
faq.answer: We start from the real sales process, not the feature catalog — the Adoption criterion is evaluated from day one, together with your sales team, not at the end of the process.

meta.title: HCM (Human Capital Management) Selection | Cyrrus
meta.description: HCM selection consulting: we align human capital technology with your payroll, talent, and employee experience — 100% vendor-agnostic.

hero.title: Human capital management (HCM) software selection
hero.description: Human capital technology should adapt to the organization, not the other way around. We help organizations define, evaluate, and select the HCM that best fits their people-management model.

dolor.title: When people management becomes a fragmented operation

items.title: Multiple systems
items.description: Payroll, talent, and recruiting live on separate platforms that don't connect.

items.title: Manual processes
items.description: Vacation, performance reviews, and compensation managed in spreadsheets.

items.title: Scattered information
items.description: There's no single source of truth for each employee.

items.title: Disconnected payroll
items.description: Payroll doesn't communicate with the rest of the HR processes.

items.title: Poor employee experience
items.description: Slow, unintuitive processes that frustrate the team.

items.title: Systems that don't scale
items.description: The current platform can't support headcount growth or new geographies.

dolor.narrativa: Poorly integrated talent processes don't just create redundant work — they make it impossible to make people decisions with reliable data.

problemaReal.title: An HCM isn't just an HR system
problemaReal.body: It has to support People, Processes, Policies, Data, Experience, Compliance, and the organization's talent strategy — not just automate payroll.
problemaReal.punch: That's why selection shouldn't be done by comparing features alone.

solucion.title: We align technology with your human capital management model
solucion.linkLabel: This is how we apply the full CIRA Method to software selection

evaluamos.title: We evaluate the HCM from the organization's and its people's perspective

items.title: Functional
items.description: Does it cover Core HR, payroll, talent, recruiting, performance, and compensation?

items.title: Technical
items.description: Does it integrate with the ERP and the company's other administrative systems?

items.title: Economic
items.description: What's the cost per employee and the total cost as headcount scales?

items.title: Strategic
items.description: Does it support learning, talent analytics, and AI aligned with the people strategy?

items.title: Vendor
items.description: Does it comply with labor and payroll regulations in every country the company operates in?

items.title: Employee experience
items.description: Is it intuitive for employees, or will it end up underused like the previous systems?

entregables.title: A platform that can keep up with the organization's evolution

faq.question: How long does an HCM selection process take?
faq.answer: As a reference, the CIRA method's Identify phase typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, from the strategic kickoff through contracting support.

faq.question: We operate in several countries — how does that affect the selection?
faq.answer: Regulatory and payroll compliance per country is one of the six criteria we evaluate from the start — not an adjustment made after the selection.

meta.title: EAM (Enterprise Asset Management) Selection | Cyrrus
meta.description: EAM selection consulting: we choose your asset management platform based on your operation's lifecycle, with no vendor bias.

hero.title: Enterprise asset management (EAM) software selection
hero.description: Asset management starts long before maintenance. It starts with choosing the right technology. We help organizations define, evaluate, and select the EAM that best fits their operational reality.

dolor.title: When assets become a source of uncertainty

items.title: Reactive maintenance
items.description: Assets get serviced after they've already failed, not before.

items.title: Scattered information
items.description: Maintenance history lives in physical logs or loose files.

items.title: Assets without traceability
items.description: No clear visibility of where each asset is or what condition it's in.

items.title: Costs hard to control
items.description: Maintenance and spare-parts spending can't be accurately attributed.

items.title: Unplanned downtime
items.description: Failures that stop the operation with no prior warning.

items.title: Disconnected spare-parts inventory
items.description: Procurement doesn't know what parts are available before issuing an order.

dolor.narrativa: Poor visibility into asset lifecycle doesn't just cost in maintenance — it costs in stopped operations.

problemaReal.title: An EAM has to fit the operational reality of the assets
problemaReal.body: The need for an EAM looks different in manufacturing, energy, utilities, infrastructure, mining, transportation, or oil & gas.
problemaReal.punch: The EAM with the most features isn't necessarily the best EAM for a given organization.

solucion.title: We select the platform based on your assets' lifecycle
solucion.linkLabel: This is how we apply the full CIRA Method to software selection

evaluamos.title: We evaluate the EAM beyond maintenance

items.title: Functional
items.description: Does it cover asset management, work orders, planning, and spare-parts inventory?

items.title: Technical
items.description: Does it integrate with the ERP and support IoT for real-time monitoring?

items.title: Economic
items.description: What's the total cost of ownership versus the reduction in unplanned downtime?

items.title: Strategic
items.description: Does it support predictive maintenance and analytics to anticipate failures?

items.title: Vendor
items.description: Does it have real experience in the organization's specific industry?

items.title: Adoption
items.description: Will the field maintenance team actually use it, or default back to paper?

entregables.title: A solution that connects assets, operations, and the business
entregables.closingQuote: A technology recommendation backed by operational, technical, economic, and strategic requirements — not just maintenance features.

faq.question: How long does an EAM selection process take?
faq.answer: As a reference, the CIRA method's Identify phase typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, from the strategic kickoff through contracting support.

faq.question: Does the evaluation account for my operation's specific industry?
faq.answer: Yes — the Vendor criterion includes evaluating real experience in industries like manufacturing, energy, mining, or transportation, not just generic platform capability.
